title: Reply: tradition is as silent — lost-tradition retorsion mirrors the lost-books attack
source_text: XVII. Respondeo illo argumento, si aliquid virium habet, posse probari non tantum Scripturam non continere omnia scitu necessaria, sed totam fidei doctrinam non posse sufficienter hauriri ex Scriptura sacra & traditione non scripta simul sumptis. Etenim hic non minus tacet traditio & verbum non scriptum quam Scriptura sacra. Alioqui depromant nobis Pontificii ex traditione sua quodnam fuerit illud remedium peccati originalis sub Veteri Testamento in foeminis & masculis morientibus ante octavum diem. Quod si dicant traditionem illam intercidisse, retorquebitur in illos argumentum istud quo probare nituntur Scripturam sacram non esse sufficientem fidei regulam, quoniam, ut putant, quidam Scripturae libri perierunt. Et pari facilitate poterit dici hoc fuisse contentum in quodam ex istis libris propheticis quos interiisse contendunt.
pass_a_gloss: I reply that by that argument, if it has any force, it can be proved not only that Scripture does not contain all things necessary to be known, but that the whole doctrine of faith cannot be sufficiently drawn from sacred Scripture and unwritten tradition taken together. For here tradition and the unwritten word are no less silent than sacred Scripture. Otherwise let the Pontiffs produce for us from their tradition what that remedy of original sin under the Old Testament was in women and in males dying before the eighth day. But if they say that tradition has perished, that argument by which they try to prove sacred Scripture is not a sufficient rule of faith — because, as they think, certain books of Scripture have perished — will be turned back upon them. And with equal ease it could be said that this was contained in one of those prophetic books which they contend have perished.
pass_b_english: If the silence proves Scripture incomplete, it equally proves Scripture-plus-tradition incomplete — tradition is silent too.
Let Rome name the Old-Testament remedy for women and for boys who died before day eight from her unwritten word.
If she says the tradition perished, her own lost-books attack against the Canon rebounds on her.
One could as easily stash the missing remedy in the prophetic books she claims are gone.

lemmas.gloss: will be turned back on them

rejected: oral law supplies the missing rite

choices.why: Lost tradition equals their lost-books logic.
